name: OD9 — offda9.com (Off Da Nine)
_local_base_url_note: Arms the pre-deploy LOCAL render gate (added 2026-08-27, the day the engine's WSL Host-header fix made that gate actually work — before that it silently skipped itself on this workstation). All six smoke tests are same-host page renders, so all six run locally; a runtime fatal in any of them now stops the deploy BEFORE prod instead of being discovered by prod smoke after the sync.
_deploy_enabled_note: Enabled 2026-08-11 after the --dry diff was reviewed line by line. That review was not a formality: it caught that api/drip/weekly_lovelogic_sender.php (cron-driven, Mondays 9 AM) was NEWER ON PROD than in the repo, so deploying would have reverted a live weekly broadcast to a stale build using the wrong PHP interpreter. Fixed in 5b023d1 before enabling. The diff was also cut from 22 creates / 16 changes to 16 / 15 by removing five root-level duplicates of live senders; of the 15 remaining changes, 13 are prod-side CRLF being normalized to LF (verified zero real content difference with --strip-trailing-cr) and 2 are repo-ahead comment updates.
_origin_must_refuse_note: Added 2026-11-22. Read by the fleet sweep (prod-sentinel, check `exposure`), not by the deploy engine: every day it asks the ORIGIN, behind Cloudflare, for each path here beside /.git and /.env. Each must answer 403, a rule of ours refusing it. 200 is critical (served); 404 is a warning (nothing refuses it: the rule is gone or never covered the path); a redirect or a fault is a warning that says the request reached a page. One path per rule this site added that day. /sentinel-probe/.d/x does not exist anywhere, so only the dot-directory rule in .htaccess can make it a 403, which is why that rule answers 403 and not 404. It starts with an ordinary name on purpose: a missing path whose first missing part starts with a dot (/.nothing/x) is refused by the DOTFILE rule with or without the dot-directory rule, so it would be green with the rule deleted (tried first, and measured with the rule taken out). The other two were chosen because asking for them does nothing: config/analytics.example.php holds comments only, and /private/logs/security.log was a static log until the cleanup of 2026-11-22 removed it from the server. Its path stays listed as a name inside the refused folder: a missing name inside a refused folder still answers 403 (measured at the origin and on local Apache that day) and would answer 404 with the folder's rule gone, which is the difference this list exists to see. NEVER list a page that faults or acts when requested (config/bootstrap.php, an admin wrapper): the sweep's own daily question would then write a PHP fault into the server's error log, and the error-log watcher pages on new fault shapes (it did, at 02:26 on 2026-11-22, for a scanner's 68). A public smoke test cannot hold these: from here Cloudflare's edge answers 403 for all three whatever the origin does (measured 2026-11-22: its block page, for a made-up dot path as well), which is how they went unseen. tests/check_origin_refusals.py refuses a deploy if the first path leaves this list.
_topology_note: Connects AS the owning account. The retired tools/deploy.py SCP'd each file to /tmp and sudo-installed it as ultimaterage because 'the SSH user cannot write offda9's web root directly' — that is obsolete: /home/offda9/.ssh already holds an automation key, both ~/.ssh/id_rsa_automation and ~/.ssh/freshthaband_key authenticate directly as offda9@, the account owns its writable docroot, and rsync is present. So od9 needs NO engine changes; plain rsync-as-owner works exactly like the platform repos.

Both are in git history.
_remove_remote_note_2026_11_22_cleanup: The last 84 (2026-11-22, the old admin door retired). od9's admin is the shared platform's; what stayed here was a second, local-only door onto it: 65 wrapper pages under private/admin that load the platform from a workstation path, a two-file router under admin/ whose path arithmetic pointed one folder too high, and config/bootstrap.php, which the wrappers loaded. None could run on the server (requested there they faulted), and nothing deployable outside private/ loaded from it. Also removed from the server and no longer shipped: 13 mail templates under private/email-templates (the live senders read the top-level email-templates/), two SQL migrations and one log file that a `git reset` on the server left there on 2026-03-16. Before this list was written each of the 84 server files was hashed and compared with the blob git holds: 84 identical, so the removal loses nothing. Generated from `git ls-files`, not typed. private/.htaccess stays and keeps refusing the folder, so a file that comes back (a rollback restores removed files until the next deploy) is still not served.
_remove_remote_note_2026_11_22: The last 40. (1) private/admin/generate-wrappers.php said 'run once, then delete this file' and was neither deleted nor guarded: requested over HTTP it checks no login and writes 36 wrapper pages to a Windows path, which on the server is a relative one. Outside traffic ran it on 2026-09-24 (the 36 files were taken for a failed upload and cleaned up; the generator stayed) and again on 2026-11-22 at 07:50:59 UTC, when a scanner that had read this docroot's .git index asked for it. Deleted from the repo in this change; the 36 entries under private/admin/C:/ are what it wrote, by name, from its own list. The folders it made are left empty. (2) AGENTS.md and ADMIN_DESIGN_STANDARDIZATION.md are excluded from the deploy and were still in the docroot, served, from the `git reset` done on the server on 2026-03-16; the scanner was given both. (3) od9_schema.sql is a January schema dump at the docroot. The .sql rule refuses it, so it was never served, and it is now excluded from the deploy as well: a dump has no business one rule away from a visitor. NOT removable here: the .git folder that reset left behind (remove_remote takes files, and its pack's name is not known from this side). The dot-directory rule in .htaccess refuses it at the origin from this deploy on; ~/.claude/prod-sentinel/od9-webroot-containment.sh moves it out of the docroot.
_remove_remote_note_2026_10_07: includes/nav-html.php and includes/nav-styles.php were an older nav (a fixed eight-link list) and its styles. No page has loaded either since includes/nav.php took over; they were retired with the sectioned nav, removed from the repo and from prod in the same deploy.
_remove_remote_note_2026_09_14: dashboard/includes/env.php was a SECOND od9_is_local(), written 2026-09-14 without noticing includes/env.php had held that function since 2026-06-06. Both were function_exists-guarded, so nothing errored and include order silently decided which semantics a page got - and the two differed. The duplicate is deleted from the repo; this retires it from prod IN THE SAME DEPLOY, which is the mechanism to use rather than removing it by hand: doing that first took board.php to HTTP 500 until the repointed copy shipped.
_remove_remote_note: The customer/ portal was five 6-line wrappers that require_once files from /home/freshthaband/public_html/shared-platform/. offda9 cannot read another cPanel account's home, so every one of them returned HTTP 500 to any visitor — verified 2026-09-01, all four reachable URLs. They only ever worked while od9 lived inside the freshthaband account, and cross-account filesystem includes cannot be made to work; if od9 ever wants a customer portal it needs a real design (it is already a platform tenant at od9.freshthaplatform.com). Nothing linked, routed or sitemapped them. Deleted from the repo in the same change. Paths are relative to ssh.remote_base (/home/offda9).
_remove_remote_note_2026_09_01: The next 59 came out of the docroot-vcs-drift triage. (1) data/subscribers.txt served HTTP 200 to anyone who asked, with 11 lines holding 9 real subscriber names and email addresses, since February — no code reads or writes it, and the .htaccess is deliberately narrow on .txt because the site serves llms.txt and robots.txt. The 403 on data/*.json that made the directory look protected turned out to be a CLOUDFLARE rule, not ours, which is exactly the trap that hid the webroot source-disclosure class in August: 'it returns 403' is not the same as 'we deny it'. A committed data/.htaccess now denies the directory at the origin, and this removes the file. (2) public/ was a COMPLETE duplicate of an older OD9 site — 55 files, publicly reachable at /public/ (200), with its own robots.txt and sitemap.xml, and a second copy of the customer portal the five entries above already deleted. Every one of its pages exists at the docroot as the live version. (3) api/agent/test.{json,txt} are 15- and 6-byte scratch files ('hello'), and index.html is a January static page orphaned by index.php. Nothing links to, routes to or sitemaps any of them. All 59 were archived on prod BEFORE removal — /home/offda9/_od9_removed_before_triage_20260901_191014.tar.gz, 59 entries verified equal to the 59-line list that drives these paths — because a backup that cannot prove it captured what the delete removes is not a backup.

mappings._note: Whole-tree sync. The repo root IS the docroot since the public/→root restructure (commit 801668f). rsync runs WITHOUT --delete, so prod-only runtime content (guide-videos/, library/ media uploaded out-of-band, cache/, data/) is never removed.
mappings._private_exclude_note: Added 2026-11-22 with the admin-door cleanup: under private/ only .htaccess ships. logs/ and migrations/ above already keep rsync from sending private/logs/ and private/migrations/ (rsync 3.2.7 matches a folder pattern at any depth; measured on a throwaway tree that day), but this engine's own matcher reads a folder pattern as a prefix at the top, so its gates judged those two as shipping: the ignored-but-shipping gate would have refused the first deploy after security.log was untracked. Naming the two folders in full makes the engine and rsync agree here.

_ncz_media_note: ncz-media/ is a folder another system writes to (added 2026-10-06; Reel covers added 2026-10-10). Threads publishes a video only from a public URL its servers fetch, and Instagram fetches a Reel's cover image the same way, so the NCZ pipeline (NCZ-Content-Pipelines) places each clip (.mp4) or cover (.jpg) here under a random 32-hex-character name for the minutes that takes, then deletes it. This repository owns the folder; NCZ owns only the files in it. The folder's .htaccess is tracked here and ships with every deploy: it denies everything except that file shape and sends no-store. NCZ writes through a key pinned to one program, /home/offda9/bin/ncz-media-gate (NCZ tools/server/ncz_media_gate.sh), which can only put or remove files of that shape and refuses to run when the folder is missing, so deleting the folder from this repository stops NCZ loudly rather than letting it write somewhere the site does not know about. Here: the mapping excludes ncz-media/*.mp4 and ncz-media/*.jpg, so the deploy never ships a clip or cover left in the working tree (rsync sends the working tree, not the commit), and the drift gate reads those excludes as 'untracked on purpose'; the backup leaves them out but keeps the .htaccess; three smoke pins prove the rules are live. CLOUDFLARE (found 2026-10-10 on the first hosted cover): the zone's cache rule 'Cache Static Assets' (2026-03-13) overrides origin headers for .jpg and the other image extensions with a one-month edge and browser TTL, so a deleted cover kept being served from the edge; a later zone cache rule, 'NCZ media drop box: never cache' (expression starts_with(http.request.uri.path, "/ncz-media/"), cache off), restores the folder's no-store at the edge. The last matching cache rule wins, so it must stay AFTER the static-assets rule. NCZ's media_host client refuses any hosted file served without no-store, which is how this was caught; the smoke pins cannot see it because no pin hosts a file. NCZ's tests/test_media_host.py fails if any of these declarations disappears.

skip_always._doc: Human-readable summary of the exclude list above — why each class never ships.

Several of these are TRACKED IN THE REPO with local-dev values AND live on prod with real credentials — deploying the repo copy would overwrite prod's working config. The *.config.php glob deliberately does NOT match *.config.example.php, so the examples still ship. config/mail.php was on this list until 2026-10-11 and ships now: its SMTP secrets moved to the gitignored mail.config.php on 2026-08-27 (d5c37a9), production still held that day's revision byte for byte, and its code and every literal matched the repo's; only comments had changed since. Prod Sentinel found the exclusion obsolete, and release-warden reads the first deploy after it as prod-behind (skills 21f0124).
skip_always.server_config: php.ini, .user.ini — cPanel/server level, prod-only, correctly absent from the repo.
skip_always.workstation_only: tools/, .claude/, docs/, tests/, migrations/, *.py — never web-served.
skip_always.runtime_artifacts: logs/ (70 .eml mail-outbox captures from smoke runs), cache/.
skip_always.legacy_never_deploy: dashboard/includes/db.php, founding_patron_launch_sender.php and .htpasswd are carried over from the retired tools/deploy.py's `never_deploy` list. The first --dry run of this config would have shipped all three — porting that list is not optional when replacing a deployer.
skip_always.diagnostics: check_db.php and check-admin.php are DB/admin diagnostics that the first dry run would have newly created in a public webroot — the same class as the _phpinfo.php found serving on freshthaband.com. They stay local.
skip_always.ncz_media: ncz-media/*.mp4 and ncz-media/*.jpg — videos the NCZ pipeline puts on the server for Threads to fetch, and Reel covers for Instagram to fetch, deleted minutes later (see _ncz_media_note). A clip or cover in the local ncz-media/ is a test leftover and must never ship; the folder's .htaccess does ship.

pre_deploy._note: Brought to gate parity 2026-09-01, following this block's own instruction: each gate was RUN against od9 first, and is enabled only where it proved meaningful and either passed or had its findings fixed. od9 had been the least-gated repo in the fleet while carrying a database-backed dashboard, Discord OAuth and a drip mailer.
pre_deploy._cron_contract_note: Enabled 2026-09-01. It had been off here while od9 runs four scheduled scripts — the drip sender, the weekly sender, and two processors — and the linter would have reported 'scanned 0 cron(s), CLEAN' if simply switched on, because od9 keeps them in api/drip/ rather than the ecosystem's crons/. .claude/cron-contract-lint-config.json now names them, and the linter now refuses to call zero files a pass. All four are clean; verified able to fail by pointing it at a fixture with no CLI guard (4 violations, exit 1).

docroot_vcs_drift._why: Enabled 2026-09-01 after triaging what it reported. It listed 127 live files no repo tracked, and the reason that number was allowed to exist is the reason this gate matters: od9's checkout disagreed with prod for a week while `git status` reported clean, because git answers from its index cache. This gate does not ask git what changed — it lists prod's actual files and diffs them against `git ls-files`, so the claim has to survive contact with reality on every deploy instead of being inherited from a note.
docroot_vcs_drift._triage: 127 = 64 media assets (allowed below) + 3 .well-known files (COMMITTED in this change) + 59 removals now asserted in remove_remote + m44.html (allowed). Nothing was allow-listed to make a number go down; each entry below states why the file cannot be tracked.

_allow_reasons.guide-videos/*.mp4, library/*.mp3: 61 rendered media files, ~45MB, served directly. Binary artifacts of a render pipeline, not source: git would store every re-render forever and the repo would outgrow its own history. Scoped to the EXTENSION on purpose — a .php dropped into either directory is still reported, which a bare `guide-videos/` would have hidden.
_allow_reasons.images/*: Three cover/logo images that ship with releases rather than with code. Listed individually rather than allowing images/, because the repo does track images and a blanket rule would blind the gate to the whole tree.
_allow_reasons.m44.html: A 2.4MB standalone page (MONWELL 44) carrying its own `robots: noindex, nofollow`. Nothing links to it and it is in no sitemap, which is the shape of a deliberately unlisted page shared by direct link — so it is allowed rather than removed: deleting it would break a URL somebody was given, and that is not a call a cleanup should make silently.
_allow_reasons.otv-jay-da-gang/*: The OTV Jay & Da Gang delivery page (founder, 2026-10-26: "put it on the od9 site"). Generated and uploaded by the Synaptiq repo (tools/release/gang_pack.py --site upload), not by this repo: ~750 MB of song masters plus the page that links them. Scoped to the exact files and extensions, so a .php dropped there is still reported.

commands._why_remember: Added 2026-10-08: the dashboard's remember-me lifecycle (issue, consume+rotate, theft purge, membership re-check via the bot's read seam, logout) runs against local MySQL and the bot checkout's SQLite. It had crashed on stale include paths since August with no gate running it; a seam the test cannot reach is a loud failure, never a pass.

commands.name: no page wider than a phone (tests/check_phone_overflow.py: every sitemap page at 390px on local XAMPP, selftest first)

what the origin must refuse and what must stay out of the tree (tests/check_origin_refusals.py: a real file inside a dot-directory, config/, both answers of the server-only private/ rule, the retired admin door staying gone, nothing but the refusal rule shipping from private/, no tracked file that the ignore rules name, no deployable page requiring a Windows path; on local XAMPP, selftest first)
commands._why: Added 2026-11-22. A .git folder sat in the production docroot for eight months and the origin served it, because the dotfile rule matches a file's name and Cloudflare's edge hid the answer from every outside probe. Local Apache has the same .htaccess files and no edge, so it answers what the origin would. With the dot-directory rule removed this refuses the deploy with three findings; with config/.htaccess moved away, two.

commands.name: the server answers this site only through Cloudflare or from itself (tests/check_cloudflare_only.py: the <If> in .htaccess refuses a connecting address that is neither Cloudflare's nor the server's on offda9.com, www. and mail., keeps /.well-known/acme-challenge/ open, cannot be borrowed by path info or reopened by a subfolder, gives both answers by connecting address alone, and lets in exactly Cloudflare's CURRENT list, read from Cloudflare at every run, plus the server's own address; on local XAMPP, selftest first)
commands._why: Added 2026-11-23 with the Cloudflare-only rule. The server's address is public (mail.offda9.com is DNS-only and lands in this docroot), and on 2026-11-22 a scanner used it to skip Cloudflare entirely. The rule reads %{CONN_REMOTE_ADDR}, the TCP peer: the server loads mod_remoteip, which rewrites REMOTE_ADDR to the visitor, so a rule on REMOTE_ADDR would refuse every real visitor (measured on a scratch Apache with mod_remoteip). Ten deliberate breaks were each refused with exit 1: the rule removed (9 findings), REMOTE_ADDR, one Cloudflare range dropped, the ACME exception removed, the server-only clause removed or reversed, 0.0.0.0/0 let in, the server's own address dropped, a granting body, and 'Satisfy Any' added to a subfolder. Cloudflare's list is read live, so a range Cloudflare adds refuses the next deploy until the rule carries it; no answer from Cloudflare is exit 2, never a pass. What this cannot see: the server itself. After a deploy the origin is asked from the box (prod-sentinel's ssh), because Imunify360 drops this workstation's direct requests.

commands.name: the form checks this site carries are the engine's own files (tests/check_form_checks.py: the four copies under includes/form-checks/ equal shared-platform's core/ at the commit each names, that commit is current with the engine's main, all four come from one commit, and no other shipping file declares their classes; selftest first)
commands._why: Added 2026-11-28 with piece 4 of the form checks (spec https://claude.ai/artifact/4UWXZQzkUhCvdCZ9Y9b4nR). The guard in front of this site's forms is kept once, in the engine; this account cannot read the engine's files on the server, so it ships generated copies, and three separately written copies of one guard is what the band site's own file says cost it (each had a hole the others did not). The gate is the fleet's one implementation (~/.claude/skills/prod-deploy/form_checks.py, 30 self-checks, each judgment broken on purpose). It refused this site's own includes/FormGuard.php as a second copy until that file was retired in the same change. A copy that is stale because the engine changed refuses the deploy until the launcher's --write makes new copies, which are then tested and committed. No engine checkout is exit 2, never a pass.

commands.name: the purge-token tool still refuses a token that can do more than purge (tools/set_purge_token.py --selftest: a fake Cloudflare and a throwaway config)
commands._why: Added 2026-11-22. The token this deploy purges with is read from the gitignored tools/prod-deploy-config.json. A token in that file should be able to purge and nothing else, so tools/set_purge_token.py places one only after Cloudflare has refused it DNS, zone settings, certificates and page rules. This runs its selftest (26 checks; eleven deliberate breakages each caught) so the tool cannot rot unseen between rotations.

commands.name: the token this deploy purges with can only purge (tools/set_purge_token.py --audit asks Cloudflare, read-only; a warning until 2026-11-24 UTC, a refusal from that day)
commands._why: Added 2026-11-22. The purge step reads its token from a gitignored file that was filled by hand. This asks Cloudflare what the token in that file can do and refuses a deploy that would run with one able to read DNS, zone settings, certificates or page rules. It never purges. A token Cloudflare no longer calls active passes with a note (it can do nothing, and the purge step says so itself). No clear answer from Cloudflare is exit 2: a gate that could not look is not a pass. The refusal starts on 2026-11-24 because making the narrow token is a step only the account's owner can take; until then the same finding is printed as a warning.

pre_deploy._commands_note: Added 2026-10-02. od9 has no PHPUnit suite (see _phpunit_why_absent), so its first behavioural gate is three standalone scripts that each exit non-zero on a failure. They pin the contact form's fix: from 2026-06-16 to 2026-10-02 every notice went to Brevo, which accepted and dropped all 236 while the form reported success. test_mail_route.php also refuses a deploy that would keep the home-domain list only in config/mail.php, which this deploy excluded until 2026-10-11, so a fix there would never have reached production; the list stays in includes/mail.php, one definition. Ten deliberate breakages were each caught before this gate was added.
pre_deploy._first_run_findings: guardrail_lint reported 20 errors: five 6-line customer/ wrappers require_once-ing files from /home/freshthaband — another cPanel account offda9 cannot read, so all four reachable URLs returned HTTP 500. Deleted (see remove_remote). schema_usage found 5 phantom columns, every one in api/drip/processor.php: od9_drip_log had no step_id/email_to, od9_drip_enrollments had no completed_at, both its UPDATEs keyed on a non-existent `id` instead of enrollment_id, and the customers fallback filtered on a discord_user_id that table does not have. The drip mailer could not log a send, advance a step, or complete a sequence. All fixed in the same change.
pre_deploy._brand_lint_why_off: brand-lint encodes the FRESH palette (#D4AF37 gold on #0A0A0A, Playfair/Inter). od9 is a different brand with its own visual language, so the gate would report hundreds of 'violations' that are correct design. Turning it on would need an od9 palette definition first.
pre_deploy._cron_contract_superseded: This block previously read `"cron_contract": false` with the reason: '`crontab -l` for offda9 is EMPTY and the repo has no cron/ directory — there is nothing for this gate to check, and an empty gate is a green light that means nothing.' Half of that is still true and half was a limitation of the linter, so both halves are recorded rather than deleted. The empty crontab is CONFIRMED (re-checked 2026-09-01: `no crontab for offda9`, and no VC'd crontab references od9's scripts). But 'nothing to check' was wrong: od9 has four CLI cron scripts under api/drip/, and the linter simply could not see them because it hardcoded <root>/crons. It is configurable now, so the gate is ON above and scans all four.
pre_deploy._cron_contract_operational_finding: RESOLVED 2026-09-01. This previously read: 'od9's drip scripts are scheduled NOWHERE — offda9's crontab is empty, and the only OD9 drip line in the fleet is COMMENTED OUT in crontab.freshthaplatform.txt pointing at a different script in the engine.' All true. api/drip/sender.php and api/drip/event_processor.php now run every five minutes from tools/crontab.offda9.txt (committed, so cron-contract-lint's crontab cross-reference is live for this repo), verified firing clean. The queue was measured empty BEFORE scheduling — 0 enrollments, 0 drip_log rows — because a five-minute cron aimed at a stale queue mails every overdue step at once to real people.
pre_deploy._retired_processor: api/drip/processor.php was RETIRED in the same change and is removed from prod via remove_remote. It duplicated sender.php and could never have run: four phantom columns in its main SELECT. It was briefly scheduled here on 2026-09-01, which is how that was proven rather than argued. Nothing was lost — its one distinct behaviour, resolving a recipient from od9_members, already happens upstream in event_processor.php at enrolment time and is stored on the row sender.php reads. Kept in git history, not in the tree.
pre_deploy._orphan_scan_why_absent: od9 defines ZERO PHP classes (243 files, all procedural), and orphan-caller-scan checks for zero-caller classes and methods. It would scan nothing and report clean — the vacuous-pass shape this ecosystem keeps getting bitten by.
pre_deploy._phpunit_why_absent: od9 has no test suite. The engine's phpunit gate refuses on 0 tests executed rather than passing vacuously, so enabling it would simply block every deploy. A suite is the real prerequisite.

post_deploy_smoke_tests._note: CLEAN-URL PIN, not a page pin: /atlas works only through the .htaccess RewriteRule, and this URL is printed in a published YouTube description. The 2026-08-27 catch-up deploy shipped a rule-less .htaccess over prod's hotfixed one and this link 404'd for ~20 minutes while smoke passed 6/6 — because every test pinned a real file and none pinned a REWRITE. An .htaccess regression must fail the deploy, not be discovered by a viewer.

REDIRECT PIN, followed end-to-end: /epk on the brand domain 302s to od9.freshthaplatform.com/epk, the platform-rendered press kit (Phase 24B). follow_redirects is the default, so this asserts the WHOLE chain — the .htaccess rule exists AND the redirect target actually renders a press kit. Both custom domains 404'd on /epk until 2026-08-27 while the platform subdomains served fine; a brand-domain URL someone puts on a flyer must not depend on nobody testing it.

post_deploy_smoke_tests._why: The ledger renders from data/manifesto-map.json and includes head.php, which redefines a helper this page also uses. That collision printed a TypeError INTO the page body on 2026-09-08 while still returning 200 — so the status alone said healthy. must_not_contain is what actually catches that class; must_contain proves the map data rendered rather than the page falling back to its 503 stub.

Every page reports its own JS faults via includes/head.php. If that script tag ever stops rendering, the whole site goes silent again and nothing else would say so — the failure mode of a reporter is silence, which looks exactly like health. Checking a page OTHER than the Atlas proves the shared head carries it. Since 2026-10-08 the same page also proves the shared top bar and footer carry the collective's three profiles.

The short link an end card is read off a screen, so it is pinned on the hop rather than followed: what can break is the redirect and its TARGET, and following it would land on the Atlas and pass even if the query the whole link exists to carry had been dropped. A REDIRECT and not an internal rewrite like /atlas, because the tour is started by JavaScript reading location.search — an internal rewrite leaves the browser's query empty and the clean link lands on a map that sits there doing nothing.

The second rule is a SHAPE (all|arc[1-9]) rather than a list of ids, so adding arc5 needs no edit — and a shape is exactly what a careless edit collapses into a literal without anyone noticing, because /tour itself would keep working.

The Atlas's third zoom level is a DOOR: a lit section links into the lesson at #sec-N, and the click path that repoints those links shipped 2026-09-10. atlas_checks proves the anchors exist on LOCALHOST; nothing proved the deployed lesson carried them until someone curled it by hand after the deploy. sec-1 and sec-3 pin both ends of ch5's three sections, so a lesson re-render that drops the ids fails the deploy instead of shipping a door that opens onto the top of the page.

MAP-DATA PIN, separate from the clean-URL pin above. The Atlas inlines data/manifesto-map.json server-side (data/ is web-blocked, so the file itself cannot be smoked), and the map is rebuilt on every manifesto merge. 'Future Deployments' is the campaign's final node (V·6, 2026-09-10): its presence proves the deployed map is the 52-chapter one and not the pre-campaign file rsync would silently leave in place if the JSON were ever excluded. Update this string only when the map's newest node changes.

NCZ DROP-BOX PIN, deny half (see _ncz_media_note). The file does not exist, so without ncz-media/.htaccess this URL would answer 404; 403 proves the folder's deny-by-default rule is live, which is what keeps anything but a video of the gate's shape from being served from a folder another system writes to.

NCZ DROP-BOX PIN, allow half. A name of the gate's shape must get past the deny and reach the filesystem, so an absent one answers 404. A 403 here means the allow rule broke and Threads can fetch nothing: every Threads post would fail at the container step.

NCZ DROP-BOX PIN, the cover half (2026-10-10). A Reel's cover is a .jpg of the same shape, which the allow rule must pass like the video, so an absent one answers 404. A 403 here means Instagram can fetch no cover and every Reel quietly wears its first frame again.

_smoke_note: must_contain 'Off Da Nine' on the apex proves we reached OD9 and not a parked domain or a misrouted edge — status+200 alone cannot tell those apart.

backup._exclude_note: Large out-of-band media and runtime dirs are omitted from the pre-deploy tar to keep it small and fast. They are also never written by the deploy (excluded from the mapping, and rsync runs without --delete), so nothing that changes goes un-backed-up.
